standard.title: Reflect on drama to inform practice
standard.description: reflect on their own and others' drama to inform choices when manipulating elements of drama and/or conventions to shape dramatic action
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use teacher feedback to reflect on own drama practice (AC9ADR6D02). They have not yet systematically investigated others' drama as a source of influence, or used reflection to document and direct practice development over time.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students reflect on own and others' drama to make and document informed choices about elements, conventions and dramatic action.

nodes.label: Reflecting on own dramatic action
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can reflect on the effectiveness of own dramatic action and make specific decisions about what to do differently
nodes.minimum_width: Reflect on at least one aspect of own dramatic action; identify what was effective and what would be done differently; document the reflection
nodes.typical_width: Reflect independently and in class discussion on dramatic action created; evaluate what was effective, whether the purpose was achieved, whether elements could have been managed differently; document decisions
wider: Use Viewpoints questions to deepen reflection — 'Was meaning clear?', 'How could elements be used differently for better effect?', 'Which elements worked well to make meaning clear?' — evaluate how structured questions reveal things self-observation misses
Reflect on how performance skills communicate perspectives — investigate how drama can perpetuate or challenge unequal power relationships
Develop a sustained reflective journal across a unit — trace how reflection on own dramatic action has changed practice decisions over time

response_modes.reason: Productive self-reflection in drama — going beyond 'it went well/badly' to specific evaluation of what elements worked, what purpose was achieved, and what specific changes would improve the work — is a disciplined habit that develops through repeated cycles. Students need sustained practice with the reflection cycle, not more dramatic contexts.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one aspect that was effective and one that would be done differently
Reflection is specific — connected to elements and dramatic action, not just general impressions

nodes.label: Seeking and using feedback
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can seek, accept and respond to feedback to inform choices about elements and conventions in own drama
nodes.minimum_width: Seek and respond to at least one piece of feedback; document how the feedback changes a specific choice in own drama
nodes.typical_width: Seek, accept and respond to feedback from peers and teachers; use Viewpoints questions to generate specific feedback about elements and conventions; document how feedback informs choices
wider: Use Viewpoints questions to generate feedback from observers — 'How did the performer use language/movement to make character believable?', 'What relationships did you observe between characters?' — evaluate how each question reveals different dimensions of the drama
Develop criteria for giving and receiving useful drama feedback — distinguish feedback that identifies specific dramatic choices from feedback that is merely evaluative
Compare feedback from multiple sources (self, peer, teacher, video) — evaluate what each source reveals that others miss

response_modes.reason: Students commonly receive feedback passively without reasoning through how it applies to specific dramatic choices. Scaffolding the process — what is the feedback pointing to, what specific choice is at stake, what would I change and why — builds the habit of productive feedback integration rather than vague acknowledgment.

success_criteria: Responds to at least one piece of feedback with a documented change
Explains what the feedback revealed about a specific dramatic choice
Change is specific — connected to elements or conventions, not just 'I tried harder'

nodes.label: Developing understanding of character and human behaviour
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop understanding of human behaviours and emotions to inform authentic portrayal of characters and relationships in drama
nodes.minimum_width: Use observation and recall of human behaviour to inform at least one aspect of character portrayal; describe what the observation revealed about how to adapt performance skills
nodes.typical_width: Develop understanding of human behaviours and emotions through observation and recall; adapt facial expression, posture, gesture, movement and voice to portray age, power or attitude; apply this to character work with appropriate boundaries
wider: Investigate how to express character relationships through vocal dynamics, eye contact, distance and space — develop a vocabulary for physical and vocal relationship expression
Reflect on how performance skills can communicate perspectives about power relationships — evaluate how drama practitioners have used performance to challenge oppression
Develop understanding of how to portray characters from different cultural or historical contexts with empathy and respect — investigate what research and understanding is needed

response_modes.reason: This node integrates vocal skills (D01 Node 1), physical skills (D01 Node 2), and feedback-informed reflection (Nodes 1-2) into a coherent understanding of character and human behaviour. Students who can demonstrate individual performance skills but cannot use them to build an authentic and respectful character portrayal have not integrated the components.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The power relationships direction — how performance skills communicate and can challenge unequal power and oppression — is genuinely rich. It connects drama to social and political function, giving advancing students a more sophisticated understanding of what drama can do beyond entertainment. This direction also connects to the ICIP and empathy threads across E01/E02.
success_criteria: Uses observation or recall to inform at least one aspect of character portrayal
Adapts at least one performance skill to portray character with authenticity
Portrayal demonstrates empathy and appropriate boundaries
